item.title: The $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree of some lollipop GBS groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.14204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We say that a group $G$ has the $R_{\infty}$ property if the number $R(\varphi)$ of twisted conjugacy classes is infinite for any automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$. The $R_{\infty}$-nilpotency degree is the least integer $c$ such that $G/\gamma_{c+1}(G)$ has property $R_{\infty}$; in case this integer does not exist, we say that $G$ has infinite $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree. In this paper, we determine the $R_{\infty}$-nilpotency degree of some lollipop GBS groups by using different approaches, such as Sylow subgroups, normal forms and presentation of nilpotent quotients, and diagrams of exact sequences. We also compute the $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree of all 2-generated lollipop GBS groups and of all GBS groups whose associated graph is a tree.
item.dc:creator: Wagner Sgobbi, Dalton Couto Silva, Daniel Vendr\'uscolo

item.title: Almost tight asymptotic enumeration of finite $p$-groups: Almost all finite groups are $2$-groups of class $2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.14509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f(n)$ denote the number of isomorphism classes of groups of order $n$. We prove, uniformly over all primes $p$, that \[ \log_p f(p^m)=\frac{2}{27}m^3-\frac49m^2+O(m), \] with an absolute implied constant. This improves the classical upper bounds of Sims (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1965) and Newman--Seeley and matches Higman's lower bound (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1960) through the quadratic term. We also prove that \emph{the proportion of $2$-groups of nilpotency class $2$ among all groups of order at most $n$, counted up to isomorphism, tends to $1$ as $n\to\infty$.} These results answer questions~22.3 and~22.19 of Blackburn--Neumann--Venkataraman (\emph{Enumeration of Finite Groups}, 2007). Our proof refines Sims' enumeration framework using graded Lie brackets, constraints on deeper commutator coordinates, and incidence and Fourier estimates for alternating forms. Normalization by changes of generating bases then determines the quadratic term in the upper bound. We also prove that all but a $p^{-\Omega(m^2)}$ fraction of groups of order $p^m$ have a central elementary abelian Frattini subgroup. Combining this concentration with the sharp enumeration bound of Bl\"aser--Li--Qiao--Rogovskyy (\emph{arXiv}, 2025) for $p$-groups of Frattini class $2$ yields the linear error term. The same presentation estimates give fixed-quotient extension bounds which, together with Pyber's prescribed-Sylow theorem and the concentration result, establish domination by $2$-groups of nilpotency class $2$.
item.dc:creator: Yinan Li, Youming Qiao

item.title: Twisted Equations and Palindrome Length
item.description: arXiv:2610.14536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Twisted equations in free groups are equations in which a finite group of symmetries acts on the free group by automorphisms and anti-automorphisms, such as inversion and reversal; moreover, the variables may be subject to rational constraints. Algorithms from the theory of equations in virtually free groups solve such equations in PSPACE, but they are intricate. Our main result is an elementary algorithm for quadratic twisted equations, which extends the algorithm of Comerford and Edmunds (1981) for quadratic equations in free groups to the twisted setting and to rational constraints. Besides deciding solvability in PSPACE and yielding EDT0L descriptions of solution sets, our algorithm computes, for every quadratic expression, finitely many parametric forms describing its values as freely reduced words. As an application, we study the palindrome length of elements of free groups, that is, the least number of palindromes whose product they are. Guided by the parametric forms that our algorithm computes for products of palindromes, we found, and then proved directly, a characterization of the freely reduced words of palindrome length at most $n$ in terms of patterns describing how palindromes are nested by twisted conjugations, thereby confirming a Catalan structure conjectured by the second author. Consequently, these words form a context-free language, and palindrome length is computable in cubic time as well as in LOGCFL, answering a question of Bardakov, Shpilrain, and Tolstykh (2005).
item.dc:creator: Volker Diekert, Anna E. Frid, Silas Natterer, Alexander Thumm

item.title: Sylow $2$-Subgroups of Finite Groups with a Single Conjugacy Class of Involutions
item.description: arXiv:2610.14689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve Brauer's Problem 33 by determining the finite $2$-groups that occur as Sylow $2$-subgroups of finite groups with a single conjugacy class of involutions. Besides the Sylow $2$-subgroups arising from the relevant non-abelian simple groups in Table 1, these are precisely the homocyclic, generalized quaternion, and Suzuki $2$-groups. The classification of finite simple groups is used in this paper.
item.dc:creator: Tianze Li, Yu Zeng

item.title: Stabilizers and maximal subgroups of topological full groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.15253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study closed-set stabilizers in topological full groups of minimal effective ample groupoids with Cantor unit space. For almost finite or purely infinite groupoids, we extend the maximal stabilizer theorem of Grigorchuk and Vorobets to every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup. For a nonempty closed nowhere dense set, maximality of its stabilizer is equivalent to minimality of its stabilizer action, minimality of the regular reduction, and primeness of a canonical wide open subgroupoid. Without assuming almost finiteness or pure infiniteness, we prove spatial rigidity for stabilizers acting minimally on infinite closed nowhere dense sets. Their isomorphism types determine the ambient Kakutani equivalence class and, when Hausdorff, the effective reduction. We also realize every AF groupoid with compact unit space as the full restriction, with its relative topology, of any minimal effective ample groupoid with Cantor unit space to a closed nowhere dense subset. Combining rigidity and realization yields continuum many pairwise nonisomorphic stabilizers in every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup; these stabilizers are maximal when the ambient groupoid is almost finite or purely infinite. The realization also gives explicit AF subquotients of the ambient reduced groupoid $C^*$-algebra, including the CAR algebra, with compatibility on the canonical diagonal subalgebras.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Matui

item.title: Three-point orbits of 2-transitive groups and their combinatorial applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.15340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite $2$-transitive permutation group. We determine the orbits of $G$ on the unordered triples of its point set, together with the three-point stabilizer and its image inside $S_3$, for every affine and almost simple family in the finite $2$-transitive classification. These data classify the $G$-invariant triple systems and the simple $2$-\mbox{$(v,3,\lambda)$} designs admitting $G$, and yield in a uniform way the standard objects attached to them: the incidence and block graphs (with arc-transitivity and strong regularity in the Steiner case), the constant-weight and design codes, and the Schurian coherent configurations on triples.
item.dc:creator: Zhilin Zhang

item.title: Regular automorphisms of periodic $p'$-groups need not be splitting
item.description: arXiv:2610.15360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a fixed prime $p$, a group is called a $p'$-group if the orders of all its elements are coprime to $p$. It is well known that in a finite $p'$-group an automorphism of order $p$ is regular if and only if it is a splitting automorphism of period $p$. In the Kourovka Notebook, V.\,D.~Mazurov asked whether these two notions coincide for periodic $p'$-groups. We answer this question in the negative by constructing a periodic group of prime period $q$ that admits a regular automorphism of order $p \neq q$ which is not splitting.
item.dc:creator: V. S. Atabekyn

item.title: Minimal Product Sets in Finite Metacyclic Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.15777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Minimum product-set problems ask how small a product of two subsets of prescribed cardinalities can be in a finite group. Although the problem is completely understood for finite abelian groups, exact results in the nonabelian setting are available only for particular classes. We determine the minimum product-set function $\mu_G$ for every finite metacyclic group, without assuming that the relevant cyclic extension splits. Our proof converts the extremal problem into a finite recursive arithmetic description of the feasible cardinality vectors of subset trios. The recursion combines the subgroup structure of finite metacyclic groups with the structural classification of maximal critical subset trios. The resulting characterization recovers the previously known formulas for abelian and nilpotent groups, dihedral groups, and nonabelian groups of order $pq$. It also yields metacyclic examples in which the minimum product-set size lies strictly between the classical lower and upper arithmetic bounds for finite solvable groups. For faithful split metacyclic groups, we further show that requiring one factor to be symmetric, contain the identity, and generate the whole group can force a strictly larger product set than the unrestricted minimum. The latter constraint admits a vertex-isoperimetric interpretation on connected Cayley graphs.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Jimenez Ramos

item.title: The theory of $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations of groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.15826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the recent study of $\lambda$-fold near-factorizations of finite groups by Kreher, Li, and Stinson (Designs, Codes and Cryptography, 2026), we introduce and systematically investigate $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations of finite groups, with particular emphasis on the abelian case. These structures form a natural relaxation of $\lambda$-fold near-factorizations and encompass several related families that have previously been studied in different contexts. We establish the foundational theory of $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations, provide two general constructions, and prove several nonexistence results for finite abelian groups.
item.dc:creator: Donald L. Kreher, Shuxing Li, Douglas R. Stinson

item.title: A non-nilpotent localization of a finite p-group
item.description: arXiv:2610.16241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give negative answers to two questions of Farjoun about localizations of groups. For every odd prime $p$, we construct a finite $p$-group $G$, an infinite non-nilpotent group $H$, and a local embedding $f\colon G\hookrightarrow H$. The associated localization satisfies $L_f(G)\cong H$, showing that localizations need not preserve nilpotence and that the localization map $G\to L(G)$ need not be surjective when $G$ is a finite $p$-group.
item.dc:creator: Sergei O. Ivanov, Georgii Kadantsev

item.title: Nonarchimedean discrete groups and quasi-isometric doubles of free groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.16291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any nonarchimedean local field $k$, we exhibit the first examples of Zariski-dense, discrete subgroups of special linear groups over $k$, which are not commensurable to any lattice in the points of a semisimple group over a local field, and contain an infinite index subgroup isomorphic to a lattice in the $k$-points of a higher rank $k$-semisimple group. We prove that any Gromov-hyperbolic double of a non-elementary free group along a cyclic subgroup embeds as a quasi-isometrically embedded subgroup of $\mathsf{SL}_5(k')\times \mathsf{SL}_5(k')$, where $k'$ is a discretely valued field. More precisely, $k'$ is the field of rational functions $k(t)$ equipped with the Gauss valuation and $k$ is any nonarchimedean local field of characteristic not equal to $2$ or $3$.
item.dc:creator: Konstantinos Tsouvalas

item.title: Multivalued Groups and Schur Rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.16758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite involutive multivalued groups associated with Schur rings. Their reduced valency is shown to equal the least common multiple of the sizes of the basic sets of the corresponding ring. We prove that the double-coset group associated with a complemented subgroup of a finite group is isomorphic to a Schur multivalued group over the complement. In particular, every coset multivalued group is a Schur multivalued group. Using affine Schur rings, we construct families of pairwise nonisomorphic commutative multivalued groups over elementary abelian groups. We obtain asymptotic bounds for the sizes of these families and prove that the proportion of double-coset groups in them tends to zero.
item.dc:creator: A. V. Vasil'ev, I. N. Ponomarenko

item.title: On the local Frattini subgroup of a finite group
item.description: arXiv:2610.16821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\pi(G)$ be the set of prime divisors of $|G|$. For each $p\in \pi(G)$, choose a Sylow $p$-subgroup $G_p$ of $G$. The subgroup $\Psi(G)= \prod_{p\in \pi(G)} \Phi(G_p)_G$ is called the \textit{local Frattini subgroup} of $G$. Here, for $J \leqslant G$, the symbol $J_G$ denotes the core of $J$ in $G$. The subgroup $\Psi(G)$ is a characteristic subgroup of $G$ that is contained in $\Phi(G)$, the Frattini subgroup of $G$. We prove that $\Psi(G)$ satisfies many properties similar to $\Phi(G)$. Let $J$ be a normal $p$-subgroup of $G$ with $J \leqslant \Phi(G)$, and let $S$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$. John S. Rose proved that if $J \leqslant \mathbf{Z}(S)$, then $J \leqslant \Phi(S)$. So, in fact, $J \leqslant \Phi(S)_G \leqslant \Psi(G)$. Kaplan, Lev, Mann, and Solomon found various other conditions that would ensure $J$ is contained in $\Phi(S)$. In this article, we add a few more conditions to this list.
item.dc:creator: David G. Costanzo

item.title: On a Combinatorial Characterization of Abelian Group Actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.16880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$ and $X$ a finite $G$-set. We give a necessary and sufficient condition on $G$ for any $X$ to be determined up to isomorphism by certain combinatorial data. Specifically, if $M_H^X$ is the number of $H$-orbits in $X$, and $a_d^X$ is the number of $G$-orbits in $X$ of cardinality $d$, we characterize when equalities $M_H^{X_1} = M_H^{X_2}$ and $a_d^{X_1}=a_d^{X_2}$ for all $H \leq G$ and $d|n$, respectively, force an isomorphism $X_1 \simeq X_2$. Our main result is that this occurs if and only if $G$ is cyclic or $G$ is the direct sum of a finite cyclic group and a cyclic group of prime order. We conclude with an arithmetic application to $L$-function factorization.
item.dc:creator: Carson Gull, Arthur Illidge, Benjamin Mudrak, Joshua Park, Shaver Phagan

item.title: Profinite recognition of uniformity
item.description: arXiv:2610.17041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a semisimple Lie group that is not isogenous to the isometry group of real or complex hyperbolic $n$-space. We show that the rational rank is a profinite invariant for irreducible lattices in $G$, unless $G$ has type $D_{2n}$ which forms a genuine exception. In particular, profinitely isomorphic lattices in $G$ of type $D_{2n}$ can have differing virtual cohomological dimension. As another corollary, uniformity is a profinite property for irreducible lattices in $G$ outside type $D_4$. Assuming CSP, the existence of triality symmetries gives uniform and non-uniform profinitely isomorphic lattices in type $D_4$.
item.dc:creator: Holger Kammeyer

item.title: An explicit construction of a limit variety of groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.17086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an explicit countable group \(G_*=N(R)\rtimes A\) whose generated variety is a limit variety of groups: it has no finite identity basis, whereas every proper subvariety is finitely based. Here \(A\) is relatively free in the variety of groups of nilpotency class at most two and exponent dividing four, and \(R\) is an explicitly defined quotient of the group algebra \(\mathbb F_2[A]\). The proof establishes an ascending chain condition for coefficient spaces indexed by six ordered commutator entries and reduces every proper subvariety to a hereditarily finitely based approximation. Non-finite basability is obtained by transferring independent identities from the constructions of Gupta and Krasilnikov. The resulting variety is contained in \(\mathfrak B_4\mathfrak B_2\). This construction provides the first example of such a variety in which both the generators and a basis are explicitly given.
item.dc:creator: Zidong Gao, Yilin Zhou

item.title: On a finite group in which every non-supersolvable maximal subgroup is a TI-subgroup
item.description: arXiv:2610.17537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a complete characterization of a finite group in which every non-supersolvable maximal subgroup is a TI-subgroup, which generalizes some known related results.
item.dc:creator: Jiangtao Shi, Fanghua Li

item.title: Complete mappings stabilizing Sylow $2$-subgroups in central quotients of special linear groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.17631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A complete mapping of a finite group $G$ is a permutation $\theta$ of $G$ such that $x\mapsto x\theta(x)$ is also a permutation of $G$. Complete mappings have applications in cryptography, particularly in the design of round functions for cryptographic systems. The study of their parity has led to the question of which finite groups admit complete mappings of both parities. A useful approach to this question is to construct complete mappings stabilizing suitable subgroups, in particular Sylow $2$-subgroups. We show that, for every $n\geq2$, every prime power $q$, and every $Z\leq Z(\mathrm{SL}_n(q))$, the group $\mathrm{SL}_n(q)/Z$ admits a complete mapping stabilizing a Sylow $2$-subgroup if and only if $(n,q)\neq(2,2)$.
item.dc:creator: Shixin Wang, Shikang Yu, Tao Feng

item.title: Zero divisors in group algebras of torsion-free groups in odd characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.17662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A recent preprint constructs a finitely presented torsion-free group $G$ with a finite two-dimensional classifying space such that $\mathbb F_2[G]$ contains nonzero zero divisors. We extend this to every odd prime $p$: there is a finitely presented torsion-free group $G_p$, again with a finite two-dimensional classifying space, such that $\mathbb F_p[G_p]$ contains nonzero elements $\alpha,\beta$ with $\alpha\beta=0$. Together with the case $p=2$, Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture therefore fails over every field of positive characteristic. The new ingredients are a signed version of the parity cancellation, made possible by a bipartite random model on one side; a type design built from the projective plane over $\mathbb F_{p^3}$ with $p$ additional letters, which makes every cross-intersection congruent to $1$ modulo $p$; and a squared-word decay estimate for this design, proved with an explicit test vector. The geometric part of the argument is taken from the characteristic-two construction. The characteristic-zero case remains open.
item.dc:creator: S. V. Ivanov

item.title: Matrix Waring Problem-III
item.description: arXiv:2610.17698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $n,k$ be positive integers and $q$ be a prime power. We prove that there exists a real constant $C_k$ depending only on $k$ such that if $ \# M_n(\mathbb{F}_q) > C_k$ then every element in $M_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ is a sum of two $k$th powers, proving Larsen's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Krishna Kishore, Sunil Kumar Mallick

item.title: $\mathrm{CS}\mathfrak{X}$-groups and free constructions
item.description: arXiv:2610.17954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\X$ be a variety of groups. A group $G$ is $\CSX$ if its maximal $\X$-subgroups are malnormal. We prove that the amalgamated free product of two $\CSX$-groups with a malnormal amalgam and without any involutions is again $\CSX$. Using this, we describe conditions under which the HNN-extension of a $\CSX$-group is $\CSX$.
item.dc:creator: Omar Al-Raisi, Mohammad Shahryari

item.title: Groups with the fixed-point property
item.description: arXiv:2610.18070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose the study of the class of groups that fix a point for every continuous action on any convex compact space. Oliver completed the corresponding program of classifying the finite groups that have this fixed-point property in finite dimensions. Turning to infinite groups, the Schauder--Tychonoff theorem establishes that the integers have the fixed-point property, but this has not been shown for any other infinite, finitely generated group. We establish a local transfer principle and use it to show, as a proof of concept, that $\mathbf{Z} \times (\mathbf{Z}/p\mathbf{Z})$ belongs to this class of groups.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Monod, Omer Tamuz, Lizzy Teryoshin

item.title: The one percent property for free groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.18106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for every $\varepsilon >0$, there is $\delta >0$ such that for every probability measure $\mu$ on a free group $\mathbb{F}$, if the operator norm of the action of $\mu$ on $L^2\mathbb{F}$ by convolution exceeds $\varepsilon$, then there is a coset of an abelian subgroup of $\mathbb{F}$ with $\mu$-mass at least $\delta$.
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Breuillard, Ferdinand Jacob\'e de Naurois

item.title: Finite groups with conjugacy classes of size $2p^n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.18193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend Burnside's $p^a$-Theorem on conjugacy classes of prime-power size by proving that no non-abelian finite simple group possesses a conjugacy class of size $2p^n$ for any prime $p$ and $n\geq 0$. Based on this, we partially extend a well-known result of L. Kazarin by showing that, given a finite group $G$, the subgroup generated by a conjugacy class $x^G$ of size $2p^n$ where $x$ has odd order, is a solvable normal subgroup of $G$. If instead the subgroup $\langle x^G \rangle$ generated by such a class $x^G$ is non-solvable (which forces $x$ to have even order), then $p= 5$ and $\langle x^G \rangle/S(\langle x^G \rangle)$ is isomorphic to the symmetric group $S_5$, where $S(\langle x^G \rangle)$ denotes the solvable radical of $\langle x^G \rangle$.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Beltran, Changguo shao

item.title: A note on the proof of nonamenability of F
item.description: arXiv:2610.18360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The goal of this note is to provide a human written exposition of OpenAI's recent proof that Thompson's group F is nonamenable.
item.dc:creator: Sang-hyun Kim, Yash Lodha

item.title: Lie groups are countably representable
item.description: arXiv:2610.18464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every Lie group can be realized by permutations of a countable set, answering a classical question of Ulam. The key deformation construction originated in an argument produced by OpenAI's GPT 6 Astra during extended mathematical discussions.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Monod, Andreas Thom

item.title: When do lazy and invertible cellular automata generate all cellular automata?
item.description: arXiv:2610.18480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a group and let $A$ be a set with at least two elements. A lazy cellular automaton over $A^G$ acts as the identity except at the cells where a fixed pattern occurs, where it replaces the central symbol by a fixed different symbol. Let $M(G;A)$ be the submonoid of $\mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ generated by the lazy and the invertible cellular automata. We study when $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. Since no lazy cellular automaton is surjective, every surjective element of $M(G;A)$ is invertible; hence $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ whenever $A$ is infinite or $G$ has an element of infinite order. Moreover, if $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has a quotient isomorphic to the Klein four-group $C_2 \times C_2$, then $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. For locally finite $G$, and in particular for finite $G$, these are the only obstructions: we prove that $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ if and only if $3 \leq |A| < \infty$, or $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has no quotient isomorphic to $C_2 \times C_2$.
item.dc:creator: Edgar Alcal\'a-Arroyo, Alonso Castillo-Ramirez

item.title: Constructions and automorphisms of quandles
item.description: arXiv:2610.18676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that if M is an abelian group and X = Alex(M, phi) is a Latin Alexander quandle with id - phi in Aut(M), then Aut(X) is isomorphic to M semidirect C_Aut(M)(phi), Inn(X) is isomorphic to M semidirect <phi> and Out(X) is isomorphic to C_Aut(M)(phi)/<phi>. As a consequence, we obtain a description of the automorphism groups of direct products of the cyclic commutative medial quandles C_{2n+1} and the dihedral quandles R_{2n+1}, and we find their orders. Furthermore, we correct a result of Bardakov-Fedoseev [Algebra and Logic 63 (2024), no. 2, 111-142] on multiplication of quandles and prove that the Borodin-Neshchadim-Simonov and Markhinina-Nasybullov quandles can be constructed from conjugation, core, and generalized Alexander quandles, using the operation of multiplication of quandles. Finally, we consider the quotients of a quandle Q, namely the medialization Q^med, the commutativization Q^com, and the trivialization Q^tr. We prove that the conjugation quandle Conj(G) is medial if and only if gamma_2(G) <= Z(G); we find bounds for |Conj(G)^med| and prove that Core(G)^com is isomorphic to Core(G/<<g^3>>). We describe commutative generalized Alexander quandles and, as a consequence, find the commutativization of the dihedral quandle: R_n^com is isomorphic to R_gcd(n,3).
item.dc:creator: Valeriy G. Bardakov, Birama Sangare

item.title: Bisectors in the Heisenberg group II
item.description: arXiv:2610.13954v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Following previous work on metric bisectors with respect to the Kor\'anyi metric, we study here bisectors in the Heisenberg group $\mathfrak{H}$ equipped with the Carnot--Carath\'eodory metric $d_{cc}$.
item.dc:creator: Gaoshun Gou, Joonhyung Kim, Ioannis D. Platis, Li-Jie Sun

item.title: The strong nonfinite basis property of $S_7$
item.description: arXiv:2610.13980v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the three-element additively idempotent semiring $S_7$ is strongly nonfinitely based: every finite additively idempotent semiring whose generated variety contains $S_7$ has no finite equational basis. This answers Problem~1.2 in Yue, Ren and Gao's paper Explicit equational bases for the power semirings of $S_7$ affirmatively. The proof combines a rigidity property of set systems with private points and a probabilistic construction derived from semilinear sets of letter counts in finite semigroups. The argument allows arbitrary polynomial substitutions and does not assume commutative multiplication. As consequences, both power semirings of the multiplicative reduct of $S_7$, and both power semirings of every finite group of order at least three, are strongly nonfinitely based. All algebras are considered in the signature $(+,\cdot)$ without nullary operations.
item.dc:creator: Lili Wang, Qingrui Yin, Aifa Wang

item.title: $n$-Valued Analogue of Abel's Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.14044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Abel's classical theorem shows that a continuously differentiable one-dimensional associative law with a two-sided unit is locally equivalent to addition under a change of coordinate. We prove an $n$-valued analogue in the algebraic and formal settings. Over a field of characteristic zero, every associative algebraic $n$-valued monoid on $\mathbb P^1$ with a strong two-sided unit is commutative. Over a reduced commutative $\mathbb Q$-algebra, any one-dimensional formal $n$-valued group is commutative. We then classify $n$-valued formal groups over arbitrary $\mathbb Q$-algebras that are integral domains: for any $n$-valued formal group there is a unique divisor $m$ of $n$ such that the law is strongly isomorphic to the $n/m$-fold diagonal of the cyclic elementary $m$-valued law $\mathbb G_m$. This proves Kholodov's classification conjecture over integral domain $\mathbb Q$-algebras.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Kornev

item.title: Strong nonfinite basability of the three-element flat semiring $S_7$
item.description: arXiv:2610.14068v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the three-element flat semiring $S_7$ is strongly nonfinitely based within the class of additively idempotent semirings. More generally, let $\mathcal N$ be the subvariety of $\Var(S_7)$ defined by $x^2y\approx x^2$. For every finite ai-semiring $A$, each variety $\mathcal W$ satisfying $\mathcal N\subseteq\mathcal W\subseteq\Var(A)$ has infinite axiomatic rank.
item.dc:creator: Mengya Yue, Xiaolei Shao

item.title: Transposition Cayley Spectra and Subgraph Counts
item.description: arXiv:2610.14373v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on the vertex set $[n]$, and let $\Gamma(G)$ be the Cayley graph of the symmetric group $S_n$ generated by the transpositions corresponding to the edges of $G$. We study the inverse spectral problem for the assignment $G\mapsto \Gamma(G)$ through the group-algebra operator $A_G=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}(ij)$ and its regular spectral moments $M_k(G)=\operatorname{tr}(A_G^k)$. The moments admit two all-order forms: a universal support expansion in non-induced subgraph counts of $G$, and a representation-theoretic expansion over the irreducible representations of $S_n$. We compute the first nontrivial moments through order six. In particular, the fourth moment already contains the Coxeter triangle relation and determines the signed local invariant $6N_{K_3}(G)-N_{P_3}(G)$, rather than $N_{P_3}(G)$ alone. Consequently, for triangle-free graphs the spectrum determines the second moment of the degree sequence. We also give a simplified sixth-moment formula for triangle-free graphs, showing that in this class the spectrum determines $5N_{K_{1,3}}(G)+2N_{P_4}(G)+12N_{C_4}(G)$. Further structural consequences include bipartiteness and spectral symmetry of $\Gamma(G)$, a precise connectedness test, and the identification of the standard irreducible component with the shifted graph Laplacian $mI-L_G$.
item.dc:creator: Boris Shapiro

item.title: Clifford Invariants and Three-Copy Quantum Tests
item.description: arXiv:2610.14758v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an explicit treatment of the third tensor power of the Clifford representation on $n$ qutrits, for $n\geq2$. This representation has five pairwise inequivalent irreducible constituents, with multiplicities $1,1,1,1,2$. The decomposition reduces the Clifford twirl of a tensor cube to four real parameters. Two of them are spectral moments of the input. The other two are cubic invariants expressed as sums of cubes of the Weyl characteristic function and the discrete Wigner function. On trace-one Hermitian matrices, the invariant polynomials of degree at most three are spanned by the constant function and four algebraically independent functions. These functions do not separate Clifford orbits. For pure inputs a single parameter suffices. We recover its range and the characterization of its maximum by stabilizer states. We bound the stabilizer fidelity, determine full separability across the three copies in the symmetric family, and recover the criterion for a complex projective $3$-design. We classify the jointly invariant quantum Boolean functions. For stabilizer testing and for testing unknown observables we give explicit bounds on copies and queries. We also give character formulas for the finite projective Clifford groups and record the complete character table for two qutrits.
item.dc:creator: Xingya Fan, Yongzhi Luan

item.title: A quotient of the Bruhat-Tits building classifying maximal matrix orders over curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.15147v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a previous work, we defined a quotient graph of the Bruhat-Tits tree associated to the degree two special linear group over a local field whose vertex set is in correspondence with the maximal orders in a certain number of spinor genera. This graph has been applied to the study of the structure of some arithmetic groups, their presentations and their (co)homology groups. The genera of Eichler orders, which, for instance, are related to the problem of finding a basis that simultaneously splits two vector bundles with the same generic fiber, can often be described in terms of simpler genera via quotients. Furthermore, some embedding problems of orders can be studied via quotient graphs. These results provide a geometric framework for the study of maximal orders over function fields. In this article, we extend that construction to a higher dimensional setting through the use of singular chain complexes. Then we describe the set of vertices in this quotient that correspond to split maximal orders and the topology of the corresponding region of the quotient complex. More precisely, we show that these ``split vertices'' fall into a finite number of quotients of apartments by suitable subgroups of the corresponding Weyl group, the symmetric group. We relate these ``quotient apartments'' with the cuspidal sectors defined by previous authors who studied the quotient by the group of integral points of the special linear group. Both quotients are indeed related by a ramified cover that is unramified on cusps, as proved here.
item.dc:creator: Luis Arenas-Carmona, Claudio Bravo, Ignacio Saavedra

item.title: Answer some Tkachenko's questions in factorizable semitopological groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.15385v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a Hausdorff quasitopological abelian group that is second-countable and semiregular, with a bounded continuous function that does not factor through any regular first-countable semitopological group. Its regular and Tychonoff reflections coincide, have a countable network, and fail even factorizability through arbitrary first-countable semitopological groups. This gives negative answers to \cite[Problems~6.1, 6.2, 6.4, and~6.5]{Tk2026} of Tkachenko. The construction starts with a countable cone group whose common separation reflection is not Fr\'echet--Urysohn, answering \cite[Problems~6.8 and~6.9]{Tk2026} negatively. In contrast, symmetrization gives affirmative answers to \cite[Problems~6.6 and~6.7]{Tk2026} without separation assumptions. We also show that every countable semitopological group admits simultaneous factorizations of countable families through second-countable Tychonoff semitopological groups.
item.dc:creator: Li-Hong Xie

item.title: Continuum-many discontinuous actions of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.15653v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For any $n\geq 1$, we construct a continuum of non-conjugate actions by homeomorphisms of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on the $n$-sphere $S^{n}$ that do not extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{R})$. We do this by adapting a blow-up construction of Bowden and Mann. We motivate studying these actions and note down some related observations.
item.dc:creator: Segev Gonen Cohen

item.title: Stable reduction and large Nielsen orbits on generalized Markoff surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16407v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish lower bounds on the orbit cardinalities of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ on the $\mathbb{F}_p$-points of the generalized Markoff surfaces given by $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xyz = \tau+2$. We show that outside of the reductions of a certain exceptional finite set of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$-points found by Dubrovin and Mazzocco, every orbit has cardinality $\ge p$. Together with a recent result of Nathaniel Kingsbury-Neuschotz, this establishes, for all but finitely many primes $p$, the classification conjectures of McCullough-Wanderley (2013), and gives a complete classification of the connected components of the Hurwitz stack of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of elliptic curves, only branched above the origin. This extends earlier work of Bourgain-Gamburd-Sarnak and the author in the Markoff case $\tau = -2$. Our method studies certain noncongruence modular curves attached to a $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$-orbit. These modular curves parametrize elliptic curves with a $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-cover. We use this moduli interpretation to show that the noncongruence modular curves involved have bad reduction, as a cover of the $j$-line, at some place above $p$. This implies that the degree of the cover is $\ge p$, which translates into the desired bound on orbits. Key inputs include a result of Bouw-Wewers on bad reduction of three-point $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of the projective line, and the general stable reduction theory of Henrio, Obus, Raynaud, and Wewers.
item.dc:creator: William Y. Chen

item.title: Entropy, isoperimetry and the total variation profile of random walks
item.description: arXiv:2610.16834v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The total variation profile $\mathrm{TV}_n$ of a random walk measures how far its distribution at time $n$ is from being invariant under the generators. Three lower bounds are given: an elementary bound $\mathrm{TV}_n \geq 1/\big(44\,L(n)\big)$ in terms of the speed $L(n)$; a bound by the entropy increment $H(P^{n+1}) - H(P^n)$, which is a reverse Pinsker inequality; and a bound in terms of the entropy and the isoperimetric profile. Deciding whether the entropy-increment bound always improves on the isoperimetric one is related to conjectures on the growth of the entropy and of groups. The motivation comes from the question of whether the distributions of a random walk can be transported back onto their translates at bounded cost.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Gournay

item.title: Classifying quasi-representations of groups via their characters
item.description: arXiv:2610.17196v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every countable discrete group, we construct a character for finite-dimensional unitary quasi-representations, with values in the inverse limit of the equivariant $K$-theory of its Rips complexes. The character is a complete invariant for quasi-representations up to stable equivalence for amenable groups and, more generally, for groups satisfying the Haagerup property and QR-quasidiagonality. For Haagerup groups satisfying quantitative QR-quasidiagonality, we also obtain a quantiative version of the theorems. These conclusions apply when the maximal group $C^*$-algebra is quasidiagonal and has the lifting property, including amenable groups, free groups, and closed orientable surface groups. For surface groups, rank and winding number give complete invariants for the classification. Finally, composing with the equivariant Chern character gives a delocalized cohomological obstruction to stable equivalence of a quasi-representation with genuine representations.
item.dc:creator: Shmuel Weinberger, Jianchao Wu, Guoliang Yu

item.title: A characterization of central extensions relative to n-nilpotent objects
item.description: arXiv:2610.17389v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterize the central extensions, in the sense of the categorical theory of central extensions of Janelidze and Kelly, relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of $n$-nilpotent objects of a semi-abelian and algebraically coherent category. An extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ turns out to be central precisely when the iterated Huq commutator $[A,[A,\dots,[A,K]\dots]]$, with $n$ occurrences of $A$, vanishes. For $n=2$ this condition reads $[A,[K,A]] = 0$, that is, $[K,A]$ is a central subobject of $A$. In the special case of groups this description was obtained by Everaert and the first author. The present proof is categorical, and applies in particular to Lie algebras, to crossed modules, to cocommutative Hopf algebras over a field, and to any category of interest.
item.dc:creator: Marino Gran, James R. A. Gray

item.title: Quandles with isomorphic representation categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.17769v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give two types of examples where two non isomorphic finite quandles have isomorphic enveloping groups. This implies that two non-isomorphic finite quandles can share isomorphic representation categories (as additive and tensor categories simultaneously).
item.dc:creator: Mohamad Maassarani

item.title: Learning a Group Element from Its Action: Galois Correspondences, Optimal ERM, and an Abel-Ruffini Threshold for the Natarajan Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.18154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study learning an unknown element $g$ of a group acting with finite orbits on a countable set, from examples $(x,gx)$. After a sample on $A$, the consistent hypotheses are the restrictions of a coset of the pointwise stabilizer of $A$, and the sample forces exactly the labels of points this stabilizer fixes; for a Galois group, they form the field generated by the data. Through this correspondence, multiclass dimensions become group invariants: the DS and graph dimensions equal the height, the Littlestone dimension the longest irredundant sequence length, and the teaching dimension the minimal base size. Among deterministic learners, symmetry makes empirical risk minimization optimal: on nondegenerate classes every consistent learner, whatever its tie-breaking, attains the optimal realizable sample complexity up to constant factors, and every consistent online learner the optimal mistake bound. Agnostically, every ERM's sample complexity exceeds the known lower bound by at most the DS-to-Natarajan ratio, up to constants. For finite Galois extensions of countable fields, the Natarajan dimension equals a group invariant, the coset-cube number, which is at least the number of complemented factors of any chief series of any subgroup. Hence the dimensions coincide for every solvable Galois group, while for the groups $A_5$ and $S_5$ of the quintic they are $2<3$ and $3<4$, and $A_5$ is the smallest group with a gap. For the Galois group $S_n$ of the general equation of degree $n$, they coincide exactly when $n\le 4$, i.e., in characteristic zero, exactly when the equation is solvable by radicals; the implication is one-way, as the simple group $\mathrm{PSL}(2,8)$ has no gap. For linear, orthogonal and unitary maps of $\mathbb R^d$ or $\mathbb C^d$ both dimensions equal $d$, and a two-fibered pseudo-cube is a disjoint union of Natarajan cubes exactly when its monodromy group is abelian.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyu Li

item.title: The group generated by a graph's derangements
item.description: arXiv:2610.18463v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the leap group of a graph, the subgroup of the symmetric group on the vertex set generated by graph derangements. We summarize historical results on graph derangements, which we call hops, and prove additional existence and complexity results. The leap groups of various canonical graphs are computed, and their behavior under basic graph operations is analyzed. We offer partial results on which groups can appear as leap groups, and study hops and leaps for infinite and directed graphs.
item.dc:creator: Mark Schachner, Gabe Udell

item.title: Balls in groups: volume, structure and growth
item.description: arXiv:2403.02485v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a fine-scale structural theory for balls of polynomial volume in finitely generated groups. Our main result shows that a polynomial-volume hypothesis on a single ball implies that every larger ball can, after quotienting by a certain canonical finite normal subgroup, be embedded in a lattice of a Lie group whose connected component is nilpotent with sharply bounded index and dimension. These Lie groups and lattices form chains of successive quotients that are essentially unique, giving a quantitative fine-scale analogue of Losert's strengthening of the Mal'cev completion. This describes the fine structure of the group with sharp algebraic and quantitative precision; for example, it leads to sharp bounds in Breuillard, Green and Tao's finitary version of Gromov's polynomial-growth theorem. These results have a wide range of applications in various aspects of the theory of vertex-transitive graphs, including for instance random walks, percolation, and scaling limits. We obtain some of these applications in the present paper, and treat others in companion papers. Some are due to or joint with other authors.
item.dc:creator: Romain Tessera, Matthew Tointon

item.title: Asymptotics of rational representations for algebraic groups
item.description: arXiv:2405.17360v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the cohomology of subgroups $\Gamma$ of an algebraic group $G$ with coefficients in the various irreducible rational representations of $G$ and raise a conjecture about it. Namely, we expect that the dimensions of these cohomology groups approximate the L2-analogues of Betti numbers of $\Gamma$ with a controlled error term. We provide positive answers when $G$ is a product of copies of $SL_2$.
item.dc:creator: Lander Guerrero S\'anchez, Henrique Souza

item.title: A fixed point theorem for the action of linear higher rank algebraic groups over local fields on symmetric spaces of infinite dimension and finite rank
item.description: arXiv:2505.05220v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let F be a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero whose residue field has at least three elements. Let G be an almost simple linear algebraic group over F, with rank_F(G) >= 2. Let X be a simply connected symmetric space of infinite dimension and finite rank, with non-positive curvature operator. We prove that every continuous action by isometries of G on X has a fixed point. If the group G contains SL_3(F), the result holds without any assumption on the non-archimedean local field F. The result extends to cocompact lattices in G if the cardinality of the residue field of F is large enough, with a bound that depends on rank_F(G).
item.arxiv:journal_reference: International Mathematics Research Notices, Volume 2026, Issue 20, October 2026, rnag229
item.dc:creator: Federico Viola

item.title: The average-case complexity of the Word Problem for groups of matrices over~$\mathbb{Q}$ is linear
item.description: arXiv:2506.00948v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the Word Problem in finitely generated subgroups of $\textsf{GL}_d(\mathbb{Q})$ can be solved in linear average-case complexity, both when the input words are chosen uniformly at random among the words of a given length and when they are chosen uniformly at random among the reduced words of a given length. This is done under the bit-complexity model, which accounts for the fact that large integers are handled (as numerators and denominators of rational numbers). Corollaries include the fact that the Word Problem can be solved in linear average-case complexity for finitely generated nilpotent or polycyclic groups. Our result also generalizes to matrices in $\textsf{GL}_d(R)$, where $R$ is an algebraic number field. And we show that no algorithm can solve this problem in sublinear worst-case or average-case complexity.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'erique Bassino, Vincent Jug\'e, Cyril Nicaud, Pascal Weil

item.title: On the linearity of fundamental groups of certain graphs of groups
item.description: arXiv:2506.09213v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study linearity over $\mathbb{Z}$ for fundamental groups of finite graphs of groups. Using embeddings into right-angled Artin groups and passage to finite-index subgroups, we establish sufficient conditions for integral linearity of multiple HNN extensions and of star graphs of groups with a free or free abelian central vertex group, free abelian leaf groups, and cyclic edge groups. We also prove that every amalgamated free product of two finitely generated free abelian groups is virtually a right-angled Artin group, and hence $\mathbb{Z}$-linear. Finally, we recover the characterization that a non-elementary generalized Baumslag--Solitar group is $\mathbb{Z}$-linear if and only if its modular homomorphism has image contained in $\{1,-1\}$.
item.dc:creator: D. Tsipa

item.title: Harmonic projections, recurrent extensions and stability of the Liouville property
item.description: arXiv:2602.00187v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Liouville property is a strong form of amenability, but contrary to amenability, it is not well-behaved under extensions. In this paper it is shown that, for every probability measure whose support generates the group as a semigroup, bounded harmonic functions are constant on the cosets of the FC-hypercentre, and more generally of any normal subgroup generated by elements whose centraliser is a recurrent set for the random walk; iterating this construction yields the hyperrecurrent subgroup. Hence the Liouville property passes to hyperrecurrent extensions; this applies for instance to many metabelian groups, to Houghton's groups and to permutational wreath products. For [FC-]hypercentral extensions, measures whose support only generates the group are also considered, using a projection from $\ell^\infty$ onto the space of harmonic functions. Finally, it is shown that adding to a symmetric finitely supported measure a Dirac mass at an element of finite order whose centraliser is a recurrent set does not change the bounded harmonic functions.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Gournay

item.title: Polycyclic groups and profinite isomorphism
item.description: arXiv:2605.28310v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Profinite Isomorphism Problem for a class of groups \mathcal{C} asks for an algorithm that decides for any two groups in \mathcal{C} whether they have isomorphic profinite completions. We present the positive solution to this problem for the class of virtually polycyclic groups.
item.dc:creator: Dan Segal

item.title: Quasi-isometries between graphs of totally disconnected locally compact groups
item.description: arXiv:2608.30881v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ and $H$ be compactly generated totally disconnected locally compact (tdlc) groups that decompose as finite graphs of tdlc groups $(\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{A})$ and $(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{B})$ such that all edge groups are compact and all vertex groups have at most one end. We generalize a result of Papasoglu--Whyte to tdlc groups and show that $G$ and $H$ are quasi-isometric if and only if they have the same number of ends and every one-ended vertex group of $(\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{A})$ is quasi-isometric to a one-ended vertex group of $(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{B})$, and vice versa. As an application, we construct uncountably many pairwise non-quasi-isometric compactly generated non-discrete simple tdlc groups, strengthening a result by Smith.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Giersbach

item.title: Graphical Discreteness, Coxeter Doublings and Generalized Polygons
item.description: arXiv:2609.28550v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Graphical discreteness is not preserved under quasi-isometry in general. We prove that, for every finite thick generalized $m$-gon $\Gamma$ with $m\geq 3$, graphical discreteness is nevertheless constant on the class of finitely generated groups quasi-isometric to the right-angled Coxeter group $W_\Gamma$: such a group $\Lambda$ is graphically discrete if and only if $\Gamma$ is nonflexible, meaning that no nontrivial graph automorphism of $\Gamma$ fixes a closed star pointwise. The proof combines quasi-isometric rigidity of Fuchsian buildings with a metric-strata argument that recovers the standard Coxeter Cayley graph from the building metric. For finite-rank Coxeter systems, we also show that the automorphism group of the standard Cayley graph is compact-by-discrete if and only if it is discrete, equivalently, if and only if the defining diagram is nonflexible. We further obtain obstructions to graphical discreteness from one-vertex doublings, classify compact-by-discreteness for standard chamber graphs of graph products of finite groups, and derive applications to finite projective planes and to right-angled Coxeter groups with Menger curve boundary. Our methods do not settle whether nonflexible finite thick generalized polygons exist.
item.dc:creator: Xing-Yu Hu

item.title: The van Est theorem for Rota-Baxter Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.05216v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Rota-Baxter Lie groups are the group-level counterparts of Rota-Baxter Lie algebras of weight $1$. In this paper, we first establish a correspondence between representations of Rota-Baxter Lie groups and representations of Rota-Baxter Lie algebras of weight $1$ via differentiation and integration. We then develop a cohomology theory for Rota-Baxter Lie groups with coefficients in a representation by constructing an explicit cochain complex in arbitrary degrees. We justify this theory by proving a van Est type theorem, which relates the cohomology of a Rota-Baxter Lie group to that of its Rota-Baxter Lie algebra of weight $1$. As an application, we prove that equivalence classes of central extensions of a Rota-Baxter Lie group are classified by the second cohomology group.
item.dc:creator: Jun Jiang

item.title: Counterexamples to the continuous Aldous-Lyons conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.08581v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct non-co-sofic invariant random subgroups in connected simple real Lie groups of rank one with finite center, in Zariski connected simple rank-one groups over non-Archimedean local fields, and in Aut(T) for regular and bi-regular trees T. This gives a negative answer to the continuous analogue of the classical Aldous-Lyons conjecture for these groups. Our constructions build on the existence of a finitely generated non-sofic group and answer a question raised in the author's ICM paper [Gel18].
item.dc:creator: Tsachik Gelander

item.title: Higher Brin--Thompson groups are Kazhdan
item.description: arXiv:2610.09524v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an algebraic criterion for certain sequences $(G_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of groups to have Kazhdan's property $(T)$ eventually. As a consequence, we prove that the Brin--Thompson groups $nV$ have Kazhdan's property $(T)$ for large $n$. The algebraic criterion provides a uniform proof that $nV$, $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ and $\mathrm{EL}_n(R)$ for a finitely generated associative unital ring $R$ have property $(T)$ for large $n$. In an appendix, written by Francesco Fournier-Facio, it is shown that the group $nV$ for large $n$ is neither hyperlinear, in particular not sofic, nor $\mathrm{MF}$. Further, it is not Schatten $p$-approximable for any $1\le p<\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Fournier-Facio, Roman Sauer, Eduard Schesler

item.title: Idempotence criteria for lazy cellular automata
item.description: arXiv:2610.11811v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A lazy cellular automaton $\tau:A^G\to A^G$ is determined by a finite neighborhood $S\subseteq G$ containing the group identity $e$, a pattern $p\in A^S$, and a writing symbol $a\in A\setminus\{p(e)\}$: its local rule is equal to the projection to $e$ except when it reads the pattern $p$, in which case it writes $a$. For a nonempty subset $T$ of the fiber $S_a:= p^{-1}(a)$, we introduce compatibility conditions on $p$ along the right translates $St$, $t\in T$. We show that, over every group, the existence of a compatible set is necessary for $\tau$ to be non-idempotent, and that it is also sufficient whenever $st = ts$ for all $t \in S_a$, $s \in S_{p(e)}$. In particular, compatibility characterizes non-idempotence over abelian groups, which reduces deciding idempotence to a search over subsets of $S_a$. Finally, for every dihedral group $D_n$ with $n\geq 4$, we construct an idempotent lazy cellular automaton that admits a compatible set, showing that the commutation hypothesis cannot simply be dropped.
item.dc:creator: Edgar Alcal\'{a}-Arroyo, Alonso Castillo-Ramirez, Maria G. Maga\~na-Ch\'avez, Luguis de los Santos Ba\~nos

item.title: Classes of Subgroups of a finite group with isomorphic quotient groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.13076v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the poset QIso(G) of classes of subgroups of finite group G having isomorphic quotients. Particularly, we study it for finite abelian groups and for some classes of non-abelian metacyclic groups namely, dihedral groups Dn, the group U2np and affine groups Aff(F) over finite field F. In the case of abelian groups G, we show that QIso(G) and Iso(G) are isomorphic. We show that cyclic groups are the only groups for which QIso(G) is isomorphic to its subgroup lattice. We also show that cyclic groups are the only nilpotent groups for which QIso(G) and its lattice of normal subgroups are isomorphic. We characterize finite 2-groups all of whose subgroups are q-self dual with QIso(G) being a chain. We also characterize all p-groups G of order at most p4 whose QIso(G) is a chain.
item.dc:creator: Tushar Halder, Sachin Ballal

item.title: Maps between circle bundles: Fiber-preserving, Finiteness and Realization of mapping degree sets
item.description: arXiv:2505.16285v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $E_i$ be an oriented circle bundle over a closed oriented $n$-manifold $M_i$ with $i=1,2$ and assume that $M_2$ is aspherical. We prove the following geometric realization result, which extends the classical result for maps between circle bundles over surfaces to all dimensions $\geq 2$. Let $f\colon E_1\to E_2$ be a map. If the induced homomorphism $f_*$ on $\pi_1$ sends the fiber subgroup of $\pi_1(E_1)$ to the fiber subgroup of $\pi_1(E_2)$, then there is a fiber-preserving map in the homotopy class of $f$. Using the above result and a computation of the mapping degree set of fiber-preserving maps between $E_1$ and $E_2$, we obtain the following results on the finiteness and the realization problems of mapping degree sets. ($\mathcal F$) The mapping degree set $D(E_1, E_2)$ is finite if $M_2$ is hyperbolic and the Euler class of $E_2$ is not torsion. ($\mathcal R$) For any finite set $A$ of integers containing $0$ and any $n>2$, $A$ is the mapping degree set $D(M,N)$ for some closed oriented $n$-manifolds $M$ and $N$. Item ($\mathcal F$) extends the previously known $3$-dimensional case to all dimensions $\geq 3$. Item ($\mathcal R$) gives a complete answer to the realization problem on finite sets of integers (containing 0) in all dimensions, including in particular the previously unknown cases in dimensions $ 4$ and $5$.
item.dc:creator: Christoforos Neofytidis, Hongbin Sun, Ye Tian, Shicheng Wang, Zhongzi Wang

item.title: Hilbert transforms on Coxeter groups and groups acting on buildings
item.description: arXiv:2508.18176v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study Hilbert transforms and their boundedness on $L_p$-spaces associated with Coxeter groups and groups acting on buildings. We establish new models for Hilbert transforms on these groups through the geometric objects they act on, and we show that these Hilbert transforms satisfy a Cotlar identity which was developed in earlier work of Mei and Ricard, and that of Gonz\'alez-P\'erez, Parcet and the second named author, thus conclude the $L_p$-boundedness. We manage to solve the problem firstly for the case when the Coxeter group satisfies a certain nested condition, and then extend it to any finitely generated Coxeter groups and groups that admit actions on buildings satisfying the nested condition. Our results give the first example of groups with property (F$\mathbb{R}$) on which $L_p$-bounded Hilbert transforms can be defined, and generalize the work of Gonz\'alez-P\'erez, Parcet and the second named author for groups acting on simplicial trees.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Qi Lu, Runlian Xia

item.title: Dynamics of actions of automorphisms on the space of one-parameter subgroups of a torus and applications
item.description: arXiv:2511.04111v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a connected Lie group $G$, we study the dynamics of actions of automorphisms of $G$ on certain compact invariant subspaces of closed subgroups of $G$ in terms of distality and expansivity. We show that only the finite order automorphisms of $G$ act distally on Sub$^p_G$, the smallest compact space containing all closed one-parameter subgroups of $G$, when $G$ is any $n$-torus, $n\in\mathbb{N}$. This enables us to relate distality of the $T$-action on Sub$^p_G$ with that of the $T$-action on $G$ and characterise the same in terms of compactness of the closed subgroup generated by $T$ in the group Aut$(G)$, in case $G$ is not a vector group. We also extend these results to the actions of subgroups of automorphisms. We show that any $n$-torus $G$, $n\geq 2$, more generally, any connected Lie group $G$ whose central torus has dimension at least 2, does not admit any automorphism which acts expansively on Sub$^p_G$. Our results generalise some results on distal actions by Shah and Yadav, and by Chatterjee and Shah, and some results on expansive actions by Prajapati and Shah.
item.dc:creator: Debamita Chatterjee, Himanshu Lekharu, Riddhi Shah

item.title: Companion matrices, permutations and lattice ideals
item.description: arXiv:2511.06555v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper investigates a novel connection between reductions of companion matrices associated with a symmetric family of certain binomial ideals in the coordinate ring of affine n-space and permutation matrices. Specifically, for fixed monomial orders, we observe that the reduced companion matrices yield permutation matrices satisfying group-theoretic relations. We explore the implications of these reductions, their connections to lattice ideals, and characterize the groups generated by these transformations.
item.dc:creator: Nsibiet E. Udo, Praise Adeyemo

item.title: A Generalization of Zalcman's Lemma on Complex Lie Groups
item.description: arXiv:2511.20536v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Zalcman's lemma makes significant applications in normal families, complex dynamics and many other related problems in complex analysis. It is interesting to explore a global version of Zalcman's lemma for complex manifolds, even though normality is a local property. In this paper, we establish a version of Zalcman's lemma for complex Lie groups via exponential mappings.
item.dc:creator: Xianjing Dong, Yanda Lv, Lanjuan Xu

item.title: Simplicity of action-based $C^{*}$-algebras from hyperbolic actions
item.description: arXiv:2604.12520v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the simplicity of $C^{*}$-algebras built from group actions. For a faithful isometric action of a group $G$ on a countable metric space $X$, we use the associated action representation on $\ell^2(X)$ to define the action-based $C^{*}$-algebra $C^{*}_{X}G$. We define generalized versions of the properties $P_{\mathrm{naive}}$ and $P_{\mathrm{analytic}}$ relative to this action and show that the naive form implies the analytic form. We also prove that $P_{\mathrm{analytic}}$ associated with a coefficient-separating action representation ensures the simplicity of the action-based $C^*$-algebra. As an application, for every connected orientable boundaryless infinite type surface containing a connected nondisplaceable finite type subsurface, we deduce that its mapping class group satisfies the properties $P_{\mathrm{naive}}^{\mathbb{X}}$ and $P_{\mathrm{analytic}}^{\mathbb{X}}$ for one fixed hyperbolic space $\mathbb X$.
item.dc:creator: Tianyi Lou

item.title: A topological interpretation of numbers
item.description: arXiv:2607.26926v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We survey recent advancements on the realisation problem for mapping degree sets. In particular, we explain that any finite set containing zero is the mapping degree set between some $n$-manifolds, for each $n\geq3$. Our building factors for the construction of the realising manifolds will be aspherical manifolds. Thus, along the way, we review a couple of open questions related to maps of non-zero degree for aspherical manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Christoforos Neofytidis

item.title: Minimal Cayley graphs with large chromatic number
item.description: arXiv:2608.06254v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Resolving Babai's minimal Cayley graph problem, we construct finite minimal Cayley graphs with arbitrarily large chromatic number.
item.dc:creator: James Davies, Meike Hatzel, Liana Yepremyan

item.title: Equilateral Completion in Floretion Triangular Coordinates: Locality, Product Points, and Reflection Symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2608.15925v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study unordered triples of order-$n$ floretion base vectors whose tile centroids form nondegenerate equilateral triangles. A scaled integer centroid map turns Euclidean completion into exact arithmetic on a triangular lattice, and a residue obstruction modulo $3$ shows that every equilateral centroid triangle uses three tiles of one orientation. Combined with finite triangular-lattice completion counts, this gives $|E_n|=4^n(4^n-1)/12$. Equilateral triangles containing the identity word $e_n$ as a vertex form an entirely nonlocal family of cardinality $(4^n+(-2)^n-2)/3$. For synchronized local $\gamma$-cycles, $|L_n|=(7^n-4^n)/3$ and $|L_n|/|E_n|\sim4(7/16)^n$, while on the no-$e$ support $S_n=\{i,j,k\}^n$ locality is exhaustive and $|E_n^S|=|L_n^S|=(2^n-1)3^{n-1}$. The union of the three main axes supports exactly $|E_n^{\rm ax}|=4^{n-1}+2^n-2$ equilateral triangles, split into the branches $x=y=z$ and $x+y+z=0$. For $T\in E_n$, the unsigned vertex product defines a product point $C_T$; a digitwise parity criterion characterizes $C_T=Q_T$ on local cycles and yields Fibonacci subfamilies. Multiplication-generation is equivalent to $p(T)=e_n$, hence $C_T=0$; locally this gives exactly the nontrivial global $\gamma$-orbits, and exact enumeration through order $6$ finds no nonlocal example. Retaining the signs discarded by the unsigned product gives a second classifier: a triangle has scalar vertex-sum square exactly when its three vertices pairwise anticommute. For local cycles this occurs exactly when $|S|$ is odd, giving $|\mathrm{AC}_n\cap L_n|=(7^n-1)/6$, while nonlocal pairwise-anticommuting examples already occur in order $3$.
item.dc:creator: Creighton Dement

item.title: Integral cohomology of classical Artin groups: spherical types $A,C,D$ and affine types $\widetilde B,\widetilde C,\widetilde D$
item.description: arXiv:2609.15419v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the additive structure of the integral cohomology groups with trivial coefficients of the Artin groups in the spherical families $A_n,C_n,D_n$ and the affine families $\widetilde B_n,\widetilde C_n,\widetilde D_n$. We first compute the integral cohomology of braid groups by algebraic methods and then use the Salvetti complexes to express the cohomology of the remaining families in terms of these computations. The resulting descriptions apply in every admissible rank. For each family, we establish cohomological stabilization and show that the integral cohomology groups contain no elements of order $p^2$ for any prime $p$. We also give uniform generating series formulas describing the stable integral cohomology in terms of that of the braid groups.
item.dc:creator: F. V. Weinstein

item.title: $\mathrm{C}^*$-selflessness of groups of homeomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2609.29399v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that $\mathrm{C}^*$-simple groups which admit a faithful extreme boundary are $\mathrm{C}^*$-selfless. More precisely, we establish complete selflessness of the canonical inclusion of the reduced group $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra into the reduced crossed product. In particular, the Higman--Thompson groups and the Brin--Thompson groups are $\mathrm{C}^*$-selfless.
item.dc:creator: Ryoya Arimoto
